title: Tenant-shielded metrics multiplexer and schema-normalizer for inference KPIs
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem: Inference requests emit heterogeneous OTLP and Prometheus metrics from multiple runtime components (router, runtime, sidecars). High-cardinality labels and inconsistent schemas cause Prometheus blowups and make per-tenant KPIs unreliable. We need a gateway that normalizes schemas, enforces tenant cardinality caps, propagates exemplars/trace IDs, and multiplexes metrics into downstream Prom/TS stores with backpressure and a safe fallback path.

Goal: Build a 'metrics multiplexer' sidecar/ingest-gateway that accepts OTLP/Prometheus push, performs schema canonicalization (label mapping, safe-fallback tags), tenant-aware cardinality limits, adaptive histogram bucketing, exemplar forwarding to tracing, and routes outputs to (a) tenants' Prometheus remote_write, (b) centralized metric lake for cross-tenant analytics, and (c) an SLO rollup pipeline. The gateway should support transparent canary rollouts and an opt-in per-tenant feature flag for passthrough mode.

Design notes:
- Input protocols: OTLP/HTTP (OTLP metrics and OTLP proto over gRPC) and Prometheus remote_write / pushgateway formats.
- Schema canonicalizer: rule engine (YAML-driven) to map incoming label keys to canonical keys (e.g., 'modelName' -> 'model', 'tenantId' -> 'tenant'), drop blacklisted labels, and rewrite unparseable values to '__invalid__'. Rules stored in config repo and hot-reloaded.
- Cardinality manager: per-tenant sliding-window count of unique label tuples with token-bucket style caps. When cap exceeded, gateway emits a 'cardinality_exceeded' metric and starts deterministic bucketing (hash prefix) of labels, plus emits a sampling hint to the Console.
- Exemplars & trace linkage: preserve trace/span IDs from OTLP exemplars. For Prometheus inputs without exemplars, attempt to attach trace hints if provided in headers. Exemplars forwarded to our tracing hook service for causal analysis.
- Backpressure & buffering: bounded in-memory ring buffer + disk-backed spill files per-tenant; reject with 429 to upstream if both exceed thresholds. Expose metrics for buffer utilization and rejected events.
- Routing & outputs: fan-out with configurable destinations and retries. Support per-tenant 'centralize' vs 'isolate' routing policies.
- Observability: internal dashboard templates (latency, ingestion rate, unique label counts, buffer pressure, exemplar loss) and alerting rules.

Tradeoffs:
- Doing aggressive label canonicalization reduces cardinality but risks losing rich signals; we will ship with conservative defaults and allow project-specific rules.
- Disk spill increases reliability but complicates multi-zone semantics; will make spill local and rely on upstream replay for guaranteed ingestion.

Security: gateway will authenticate upstream with mTLS and validate tenant tokens. KMS integration for any persisted buffer encryption.

Rollout: staged - start with non-prod tenants in passive mirror mode, then opt-in tenants, then default enable for low-risk tenants, finally all tenants with throttling.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway accepts OTLP and Prometheus push traffic and reports health status
Schema canonicalizer maps at least 90% of current label variants for top 15 inference KPI metrics (verified by sampling job)
Per-tenant cardinality cap prevents >75% of label explosion incidents in synthetic load tests
Exemplars containing trace IDs are forwarded to tracing hook service and can be linked in the Console tracing view
Backpressure triggers 429 to upstream within configured buffer thresholds and emits alert to SRE channel
Integration tests covering canonicalization, buffering, spill-to-disk, and retry semantics pass in CI
Rollout plan executed in three phases with monitoring dashboards validating no >5% increase in request latency or metric loss

Prototype: lightweight Go gateway that accepts OTLP/remote_write and applies label mapping - in progress
Cardinality Manager: implement sliding-window unique-key counter with deterministic bucketing fallback
Exemplar forwarding: wire exemplars to tracing-hook service; add header parsing for trace hints
Buffering: implement in-memory ring buffer + disk spill with encryption option
Routing: add policy engine for per-tenant destinations and retries
CI: unit + integration tests for protocol parsing, canonicalization, and buffering
Dashboards: create Grafana panels for buffer usage, unique label counts, exemplar loss
Security Review: schedule audit for mTLS/KMS handling
Canary rollout: deploy to staging, then mirror traffic for 48h, then opt-in tenant group
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Observability and Runtime teams. Agreed to reuse our existing otel-collector fork as base for protocol parsing.
2026-03-04: Diego pushed initial canonicalizer spec to infra-config (link in links). Decided on YAML rule syntax and hot-reload via configmap.
2026-03-07: Prototype accepts Prometheus remote_write and normalizes 'modelName' -> 'model'. Found several corner cases where numeric model versions were parsed as ints; added string coercion rule.

2026-03-10: Load test (10k tenants synthetic) shows cardinality manager keeps memory stable but disk spill triggered earlier than expected; increased default in-memory buffers and added metrics for spill rate.
2026-03-12: Security ping: storage encryption must use customer KMS key for private deployments. Added 'security_review_required' label and blocked on KMS integration for Private release.
Next: finish exemplar forwarding and add integration test linking exemplars with trace-store entries.
